description: The public BACI-VI-Bench GitHub repository provides Python code to construct and evaluate trade-network equilibrium benchmark instances from CEPII-BACI product-level trade flows. Its README names scripts for annual and sector builds, instance loading, projection-residual validation and solver experiments. The repository is MIT-licensed; the companion processed-instance archive is separately published on Zenodo under CC BY 4.0. The model represents exporter capacities and commodity flows through a variational-inequality operator and includes MARL-compatible equilibrium proximity scores. Coverage is benchmark configurations for 2017–2024 with ten exporter and ten importer slots and a single abstract route dimension, not a geocoded freight or port network. Raw CEPII-BACI annual files must be obtained separately. Fixed sector mappings, coefficient choices and source-data licences limit direct interpretation as current real-world logistics performance. A reviewer-assessed use is testing the response of trade-flow equilibria to capacity or demand shocks. model-pytradeshifts is a related trade model, but outputs and equations were not compared. No script was executed or repository archive downloaded. The code can be used in an infrastructure supply-chain simulation to assess sensitivity to capacity shocks.
